pr_title: Use ThorVG instead of NanoSVG for importing SVGs
pr_body:
ThorVG is a platform-independent portable library for drawing vector-based scene and animation.

Alternative to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/49601.

Resolves the light to dark for fill, stop colors and strokes.

https://github.com/Samsung/thorvg

Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/49205
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/16180 (Due to increased support we are able to resolve SVG issues better).
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/33641 (Changing SVG libraries replaces old bugs with new bugs.)
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/41339 (Via https://github.com/Samsung/thorvg/pull/530)
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/51763
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2912

There's still a few technical issues to resolve before this can be merged:

- There's no color conversion anymore so the light theme is broken.
- The `p_upscale` parameter is no longer respected. I suspect this will break HiDPI upscaling.
- The instructions in `README.md` for copying the sources from upstream are incomplete. We're not copying the whole `src` folder as written, instead we seem to cherry-pick only what we need (which is good), but this needs to be described so that I don't need to reverse engineer it myself on updates.

We can also update to the recently released version 0.4.0 at some point, but I figured it could be done as a follow-up.

Did some speed tests to assess if the new importer is slower or faster than nanosvg, by judging the impact on the editor start time:

### Dark theme (default, no conversion)

```
$ hyperfine -iw1 "bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64.docthread ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit" "bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64 ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit"
Benchmark #1: bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64.docthread ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit
  Time (mean ± σ):      8.598 s ±  0.812 s    [User: 7.619 s, System: 0.376 s]
  Range (min … max):    7.902 s … 10.174 s    10 runs
 
  Warning: Ignoring non-zero exit code.
 
Benchmark #2: bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64 ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit
  Time (mean ± σ):      8.781 s ±  0.505 s    [User: 7.825 s, System: 0.383 s]
  Range (min … max):    8.137 s …  9.785 s    10 runs
 
  Warning: Ignoring non-zero exit code.
 
Summary
  'bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64.docthread ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit' ran
    1.02 ± 0.11 times faster than 'bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64 ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit'
```

`.docthread` is just a build from a couple of days ago with #50864, it was merged so it should perform similarly to vanilla `master`.

So the version with ThorVG might be a tiny bit slower, but it's not really significant from my results (too much variance).
I'd say it's pretty much similar.

### Light theme (color conversion)

```
$ hyperfine -iw1 "bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64.docthread ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit" "bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64 ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit"
Benchmark #1: bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64.docthread ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit
  Time (mean ± σ):      8.781 s ±  0.307 s    [User: 7.356 s, System: 0.357 s]
  Range (min … max):    8.328 s …  9.215 s    10 runs
 
  Warning: Ignoring non-zero exit code.
  Warning: Statistical outliers were detected. Consider re-running this benchmark on a quiet PC without any interferences from other programs. It might help to use the '--warmup' or '--prepare' options.
 
Benchmark #2: bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64 ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit
  Time (mean ± σ):     11.069 s ±  0.093 s    [User: 9.509 s, System: 0.353 s]
  Range (min … max):   11.009 s … 11.305 s    10 runs
 
  Warning: Ignoring non-zero exit code.
  Warning: Statistical outliers were detected. Consider re-running this benchmark on a quiet PC without any interferences from other programs. It might help to use the '--warmup' or '--prepare' options.
 
Summary
  'bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64.docthread ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit' ran
    1.26 ± 0.05 times faster than 'bin/godot.linuxbsd.tools.64 ~/tmp/godot/projects/FreeFall/project.godot --quit'
```

Here it shows on the other hand that the color conversion takes more than 2 s when compared to the timing with dark theme, while the previous method with nanosvg was not significantly slower.

That can also be seen by changing the theme from Dark the Light in the editor, it takes multiple seconds before it's actually applied (it used to be a bit slow, but not as much).

There might be room for optimizing the way the color conversions are done in this PR. Could be left for a follow-up but we should keep track of it in an issue, for Light Theme users a startup time of 11 s when it used to be less than 9 s is a big difference.

Maybe @Calinou can get better benchmark results on a more stable system (my laptop tends to do whatever it feels like with CPU clocks).
At the computer now, will look at the new commits and optimize the color conversion (it is slow).

I pushed an update that simplifies the color conversion code by using existing `String` methods to do substring replacement, and by storing HTML code as strings in the conversion dictionary instead of doing an unnecessary HTML -> Color -> HTML conversion.

Despite the theoretical micro optimization, that seemed to make no difference at all in color conversion speed. But the code is nicer IMO :)

I need to do some more testing, I noticed that some assumptions don't work, as some files contain 3-letter color codes like `fill="#fff"`.

I restored the previous version for now until I figure this out. I think going through `String -> Color -> String` conversion does actually help support this, as `Color::html()` supports abbreviated color codes, so I'll likely keep it.

Alright, I think it's ready.

I tweaked the color replacement code to make it handle the whole quoted string instead of hardcoding support for only the `"#abcdef` format. So now it should support:
- Color codes without `#` (assuming they're supported in the spec, didn't check)
- 3-letter color codes (`#abc`)
- Color codes with alpha (4 and 8 letter)
- Named colors supported by Godot (`black`, `blue`, etc.)

comments: Godot uses the [nanosvg](https://github.com/memononen/nanosvg) library to import SVG files, and that library is no longer maintained. This means the only thing we can do is document this limitation. See also https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/16180.
